subject: Model specification for bidirectional relationship using lavaan

messages.author: d813900a8eb1ee51
messages.subject: Model specification for bidirectional relationship using lavaan
parts:
Hello all, 


I am new to structural equation modelling and I'm trying to build a SEM for my thesis. Using SEM, I am trying to find out the factors that affect people's values for ecosystems. I have specified my model as such: 

myModel <- '
#measurement model (latent variables)
socioecon =~ Gender + Age + Nationality + Race + Dialect+ Religion + Relationship + HHincomeperperson + Housing_type 
personality =~ Extraverted_Enthusiastic + Critical_quarrelsome + Dependable_Selfdiscipline + Anxious_easilyupset + Opentonewex_complex + Reserved_quiet + Sympathetic_warm + Disorganised_careless + Calm_emotionallystable + Conventional_uncreative
envtconcern =~ Limit + Modify + Interfere + Ingenuity + Abuse + NatRes + Rights + Industrial + Laws + Crisis + Spaceship + Rule + Balance + Learn + Eco_crsis
natureinteraction =~ Act_after_school_outdoors + Freq_of_visit_young + NatureAppreciation_Young + Freq_of_visit_now + NatureAppreciation_Now + Childhood_memory

#regressions
Relational ~ personality + envtconcern + natureinteraction + socioecon
personality ~ socioecon
envtconcern ~ socioecon 
natureinteraction ~ socioecon
'

which can be visualised as the following: 



An output was generated from this model, and output values seems to make sense. 

However, I realised that bidirectional relationship can exist between some of my variables such as:
1) relational values and environmental concern 
2) relational values and nature interaction 
2) nature interaction and environmental concern 

I tried to introduce these bidirectional relationships into the model by adding residual correlations into the previous model, as such:

complexModel <- '
socioecon =~ Gender + Age + Nationality + Race + Dialect+ Religion + Relationship + HHincomeperperson + Housing_type 
personality =~ Extraverted_Enthusiastic + Critical_quarrelsome + Dependable_Selfdiscipline + Anxious_easilyupset + Opentonewex_complex + Reserved_quiet + Sympathetic_warm + Disorganised_careless + Calm_emotionallystable + Conventional_uncreative
envtconcern =~ Limit + Modify + Interfere + Ingenuity + Abuse + NatRes + Rights + Industrial + Laws + Crisis + Spaceship + Rule + Balance + Learn + Eco_crsis
natureinteraction =~ Act_after_school_outdoors + Freq_of_visit_young + NatureAppreciation_Young + Freq_of_visit_now + NatureAppreciation_Now + Childhood_memory

#regressions
Relational ~ personality + envtconcern + natureinteraction + socioecon
personality ~ socioecon
envtconcern ~ socioecon 
natureinteraction ~ socioecon

# residual correlations 
Relational ~~ envtconcern
Relational ~~ natureinteraction 
natureinteraction ~~ envtconcern
'

However, I received a warning message after adding in the residual correlations 
Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.

Does anyone has any idea how I can introduce bidirectional relationships into my model? It's also my first time posting on forums so I am not sure if my question is clear enough. Please let me know if if any clarification is needed!

messages.subject: Re: Model specification for bidirectional relationship using lavaan
parts:
Thanks for replying! 

The variables that I am looking at are:
1) a subset of people's values for ecosystems (relational values) vs.
2) the extent that someone has an ecological worldview (environmental concern) vs. 
3) their interaction time with nature (nature interaction). 

Although according to the value-belief-norm theory, there is somewhat a causal path between the three: values --> world view --> behaviours. However, the relationship is not so clear in my case as the value i'm looking at is not a broad-based value but specific to ecosystems. I find that these 3 variables do influence one another at the same time. Hence, I was thinking that introducing bidirectional relationship may reveal something interesting. 

Also, I have not collected any temporal data to split my analysis temporally.

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: Re: Model specification for bidirectional relationship using lavaan
parts: Residual correlations imply that there is something driving correlation in the residuals beyond causal paths - not necessarily bidirectionally. Unfortunately, I don’t think you have a model structure where you can estimate true bidirectionally - there are no unique predictors of individuals variables involved in bidirectional paths. So, you’re going to have a hard time here. Given your additional responses, I think the question is WHY you want to have a bidirectional path, and if something like grouping and a multi group analysis would be more apropropriate here.

parts:
Thanks for the suggestion! 

I think you're right - there isn't any reason why I want to introduce a bidirectional path given that my hypothesis is to find out the factors that affect people's value for ecosystem services. Hence, it seems that suggesting unidirectional relationship will provide a much clearer picture. 

I also went to read up on grouping and multigroup analysis. It seems really interesting but I think it will not be necessary for the hypothesis of my thesis. Although I'm wondering if I can use it to simplify my model (i.e. certain socio-demographics variables can be used as group instead of incorporating them as a variable in the model)
